sources.entry: PLUR by plur-ai - Open, local-first engram memory for Claude Code. Engrams are plain-text YAML you can read, correct, and delete. The same memory is shared across MCP tools and multiple providers.

summary.one_liner: PLUR is a local-first persistent memory layer for AI coding agents, storing learned corrections and conventions as plain-text YAML engrams that are shared across MCP-compatible tools such as Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, and OpenCode.
summary.what_it_does: PLUR stores corrections, preferences, conventions, and decisions that an agent learns as "engrams" in plain YAML files under ~/.plur/, which can be read, edited, diffed, and deleted. It runs hybrid search (BM25 plus local BGE embeddings fused with Reciprocal Rank Fusion), falling back to keyword search when the embedder is unavailable. Relevant engrams are injected into agent context via hooks for supported harnesses, within a token budget. Engrams carry scope (global, project, group), polarity, feedback signals, and ACT-R activation decay so stale items fade. It also records episodes (timestamped event logs) and can sync the store across machines via git, with separate personal and shared remote modes. A local memory viewer (plur dashboard) and a memory receipt command show what was retrieved. The README also publishes LongMemEval-S recall benchmarks and points to a separate harness repository for reproduction.
use_cases: give Claude Code persistent memory of coding conventions
share agent memory across Cursor, Codex, and Claude Code
keep agent memory as editable plain-text files
sync agent memory across machines with a private git remote
inject relevant learned rules into a Python LangChain or script workflow
review what an agent has learned and delete outdated entries
how_to_run: plur init --cursor  (run from project root, for Cursor)
stack: PGlite / Postgres with pgvector (optional index tiers)
notable: Engrams are plain YAML validated against a published JSON Schema, so the format is open and portable beyond PLUR
One memory store is shared across several harnesses (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode, OpenClaw, Hermes, Antigravity, DeepSeek Harness) via per-tool adapters
Sync is git-based with a personal mode that mirrors everything and a shared mode that pushes only shared-scope, non-private engrams
Failed team-scope writes are queued locally in an outbox and retried later rather than dropped
Publishes benchmark figures on LongMemEval-S with a separate reproducible harness repository
caveats: Requires Node.js 22+ per the Requirements section, while the Install section says Node 20 or newer; the README is inconsistent on this
Needs about 2GB RAM; on lower-RAM servers embeddings are skipped and search falls back to BM25
Codex needs a manual step to trust PLUR hooks via /hooks, otherwise memory silently never loads
Some harnesses (Windsurf, Gemini CLI, other MCP clients) get tools only, with no automatic injection
The Python SDK is not yet on PyPI and must be installed from git
